solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Some letters in top of shoe box (5,4)

blocks.note: the upper is the part of a shoe above the sole

annotation.surface: Someone finds letters tucked into the lid of a shoebox.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'letters' mail and 'box' a shoebox; in fact the letters are capitals and the box is just a container.
annotation.definitionFit: Upper case is the printer's term for capital letters, so 'some letters' is a loose definition by category.

entries.clue: Disruption at university — high explosive and hot stuff lying around (8)

indicatorNotes.lying around: something turned around faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive

annotation.surface: A campus is thrown into chaos by explosives and something hot left about.
annotation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is British usage: you go up to Oxford or Cambridge and come down when you leave.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a sudden violent disturbance, the kind of disruption the campus surface describes.

entries.clue: Check under type of green fruit (5)

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, a piece placed under another is written after it

blocks.note: pea green is a shade of green
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

annotation.surface: An instruction to inspect some unripe fruit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Green fruit' reads as one phrase, but 'type of green' gives PEA and 'fruit' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the soft, downy stone fruit is one kind of fruit among many.

entries.clue: Heard about Victory in Europe after soldiers got back (9)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means surrounding, so the court verb goes round the victory letters
indicatorNotes.after: one thing after another is written later, so the soldiers come first

blocks.note: a case heard in court is tried

annotation.surface: News of the end of the war in Europe reaches troops on their return home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heard' is a court's verb here: a judge hears, or tries, a case. RE for Royal Engineers is a crossword staple for soldiers.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to have fetched something back is to have got it back.

entries.clue: Someone reviewing books theatre with 30 per cent off (7)

indicatorNotes.with 30 per cent off: a price cut of 30 per cent, applied to a ten-letter word, removes three letters from its end

blocks.note: the auditorium is the part of a theatre where the audience sits; drop IUM

annotation.surface: A critic reviewing books alongside a cut-price theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' are account books, not novels, and the reviewer checks figures rather than prose.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Books' is the accounting sense: this inspector examines a firm's accounts on behalf of its owners.

entries.clue: He easily managed, without one bit of hair (7)

indicatorNotes.managed: letters that are managed are handled and reorganised into a new order
indicatorNotes.without: 'without' means lacking, so the fodder loses the letter named next

blocks.note: one = I, the Roman numeral; removed from the fodder

annotation.surface: Someone coped comfortably, though balding.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a bald man; the 'bit of hair' is a much smaller thing than it suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: A part-for-whole definition: one lash on the eyelid is a single small hair.

entries.clue: Quietly add number to constant acceleration (5)

indicatorNotes.add: to add something to a list is to put it on the end, so the number follows

blocks.note: a is the physics symbol for acceleration
no. is the abbreviation for number

annotation.surface: A physics instruction: slip a figure quietly into a formula for constant acceleration.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Constant acceleration' reads as one physics phrase, but it splits into two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: An Italian musical direction used in English scores, meaning to play softly.

entries.clue: Basic fare no longer available with first class (5)

blocks.note: A is the first class or grade

annotation.surface: A travel notice: the cheap fares have gone, only first class is left.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price, but here it is food.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Basic fare' means staple food, and noodles and spaghetti are that for much of the world.

entries.clue: Working in a city, shy person doesn’t wind up nameless (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places one thing within another, so the working word sits inside the city
indicatorNotes.doesn’t wind up: to wind up is to finish, so a word that doesn't wind up lacks its final letter

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working
a timid person is a mouse; drop the E

annotation.surface: A timid city office worker who never makes a name for themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's shy city worker who never gets noticed is exactly what the answer describes.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from Greek for 'without a name', just as nameless is.

entries.clue: Decorated knight in love with judge (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the knight within the letters that follow

blocks.note: N is the chess notation for knight

annotation.surface: A decorated knight in love with a judge, like a romance plot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Decorated' suggests an honoured knight, but it is the definition, meaning adorned.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something heavily adorned or embellished is decorated.

entries.clue: Catch leader in town centre (5)

indicatorNotes.leader in: the leader is the one at the front, so the first letter of the word

blocks.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it

annotation.surface: An instruction to arrest a ringleader in the middle of town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Town centre' reads as one place, but 'centre' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: The heart of a place, as in 'the heart of the city', is its centre.

entries.clue: Pull up garment put on around start of winter (5,4)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means surrounding, so the putting-on word goes round the letter
indicatorNotes.start of: the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to don clothes is to put them on

annotation.surface: Pulling on a dress and wrapping up at the start of winter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' means to rebuke, as in 'pull someone up' for a fault, not to haul a garment on.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a telling-off: to pull someone up and to give them a dressing-down.

entries.clue: Sceptic occupied with bank job? (7)

blocks.note: at, as in 'at work', means occupied with
a heist is a robbery, such as a bank job

annotation.surface: A doubter busy with a bank robbery.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the loose definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: someone who doubts God is one kind of sceptic.

entries.clue: Financial expert taking one pound from fastidiously good person (7)

indicatorNotes.from: 'from' names the word the letter is removed from

blocks.note: anal = fussily fastidious; drop one L

annotation.surface: A money expert taking a pound from a pernickety do-gooder.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Anal' in the sense of fussy and obsessively neat is informal; ST for saint is the standard 'good person'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the analyst in a bank or broker's office studies markets and investments.

entries.clue: Not sorted out where to broadcast customer announcement? (3,4,3,4)

blocks.note: a store announcement is played throughout the store

annotation.surface: A muddled store where the tannoy messages go everywhere.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is taken literally; the question mark signals the whimsy. The phrase is British slang for chaotic.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom means in complete disarray; read literally, it is everywhere in a store, where a tannoy message goes.

entries.clue: Rise late with serve and be ready to attack (3,2,4)

blocks.note: to lie in is to stay in bed late
to wait at table is to serve

annotation.surface: A tennis player sleeps in, then serves and prepares to go on the attack.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Serve' sounds like tennis, which suits 'attack', but it means working as a waiter.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: an ambusher hides and waits for the moment to strike.

entries.clue: Show religious leader in rocket with American (4,5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the religious leader within the rocketing word

blocks.note: the Pope leads the Catholic Church

annotation.surface: A pontiff blasted into space alongside an American astronaut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rocket' is a verb here: to shoot upwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a long-running serial drama is one kind of television show.

entries.clue: International attempt sustains a little equality of measure (8)

indicatorNotes.sustains: to sustain is to hold up from below, so in a down clue the attempt sits beneath the little bit

annotation.surface: A global effort that keeps a little fairness in how things are measured.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sustains' is a positional instruction that only works because the answer is written downwards.
annotation.definitionFit: From Greek isos 'equal' and metron 'measure', so the definition is the word's own etymology.

entries.clue: Girls from Berkshire hosting grand spectacles (7,7)

indicatorNotes.hosting: a host takes a guest in, so the girls take the grand letter inside

blocks.note: Reading is the county town of Berkshire, an English county west of London

annotation.surface: Young women from Berkshire putting on a grand show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spectacles' suggests a show, which 'grand' reinforces, but it means eyewear.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: spectacles are glasses, here the kind worn for close work.

entries.clue: Time in cell for small thing with no charge (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places time within the cell, as a prisoner is in a cell

blocks.note: a neuron is a nerve cell

annotation.surface: A prisoner doing time in a cell for a petty offence, but released without charge.
annotation.walkthrough: The prison picture of time, cell and charge hides a physics particle, and the cell is a nerve cell.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the particle is tiny and electrically neutral, hence 'with no charge'.

entries.clue: Kit receives pay out for study break (3,4)

indicatorNotes.receives: a thing that receives takes something in, so the kit takes the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.out: 'out' as in out of order or out of joint: the letters are disturbed and rearranged

annotation.surface: A student is given kit and money for time off from studying.
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase is British: a year off between school and university, often spent travelling.
annotation.definitionFit: A year taken off before or during higher education is a break from study.

entries.clue: United Nations ignored by arbitration board displaying group loyalty (6)

indicatorNotes.ignored by: something ignored is left out, so those letters are dropped from the board

blocks.note: initial letters of United and Nations; removed

annotation.surface: A tribunal snubs the UN out of partisan loyalty.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is international politics; the answer is the adjective at the end.
annotation.definitionFit: The adjective describes behaviour driven by loyalty to one's own group, as a tribe's members show.

entries.clue: Near duo performing verse (7)

indicatorNotes.performing: letters that perform are put through their paces in a new arrangement

annotation.surface: A pair about to recite a poem.
annotation.walkthrough: An obscure word best reached from the fodder and crossings.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the rondeau is a French fixed form of poem on two rhymes, one kind of verse.

entries.clue: Cricket team somewhat jinxes second over (5)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: 'somewhat' means to some degree, so only part of the words is used
indicatorNotes.over: turned over, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words, and are read backwards

annotation.surface: A cricket side's run of bad luck costs them in the second over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' is a cricket term in the surface but here tells you to reverse. Essex is an English county with a first-class cricket side.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this is one of the English first-class county cricket sides.

entries.clue: Code for “g” (7)

blocks.note: g is the symbol for gram

annotation.surface: A cipher key: what does 'g' stand for?
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as asking what 'g' encodes, but 'for' is a piece of wordplay and 'g' is a unit symbol to expand.
annotation.definitionFit: American spelling of the computing sense: a set of instructions written as code.

entries.clue: Healing by touching arsenic regularly with bare skin (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter
indicatorNotes.bare: stripped bare of its covering, so the outer letters go

annotation.surface: A dubious cure: rub arsenic on your bare skin at regular intervals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Touching' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Its practitioners lay hands on or near the patient, so it is literally healing by touching.

entries.clue: Bar made from metal by Native American (9)

blocks.note: the Erie were a Native American people

annotation.surface: A metal bar crafted by a Native American.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a metal ingot, which 'metal' reinforces, but it is a drinking place.
annotation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for an informal restaurant serving drinks, so a kind of bar.

entries.clue: Be bigoted, losing face (5)

indicatorNotes.losing face: the face of a word is its front, so it loses its first letter

annotation.surface: A bigot is publicly humiliated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Be bigoted' reads as one command, but 'Be' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the verb sense of having being: 'I think, therefore I am'.

entries.clue: Vote concludes dead rubber (5)

indicatorNotes.concludes: to conclude is to come at the end, so the vote goes last

blocks.note: as in 'the late king', meaning the dead king
a cross on a ballot paper

annotation.surface: A deciding vote settles a meaningless final match.
annotation.walkthrough: A dead rubber is a sports match played after the series is already decided; here the words split, and rubber is the material.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by source: the milky sap of rubber trees is what natural rubber is made from.

entries.clue: Ordinary state, and not country with vacated territory (9)

indicatorNotes.vacated: a vacated building is emptied, so the word loses everything between its outer letters

annotation.surface: A political note on a state that is not quite a country, with an abandoned territory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests a nation, which 'country' and 'territory' reinforce, but it is a condition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the condition of being normal is the ordinary state of affairs.
